result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked high-visibility crosswalk with signalization located under a large bridge structure. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the overhead structure creates significant shadows and potential visibility challenges for both drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Low visibility under bridge
hazards.description: The overhead bridge structure creates deep shadows that may make pedestrians less visible to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and midground under the blue steel structure

hazards.name: Vegetation obstruction
hazards.description: Dense trees and bushes on the right side of the crossing may partially obscure pedestrians from the view of drivers approaching from that direction.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the crosswalk landing

interventions.title: Under-bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity LED lighting under the bridge structure to illuminate the crosswalk and sidewalk areas.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a large elevated structure with massive support pillars that create significant visual obstructions for all road users. While a sidewalk and a dedicated bus/bike lane are present, the overall crossing distance is very wide, and the environment is heavily prioritized for vehicular throughput.

hazards.name: Structural Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars supporting the elevated structure obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and motorists at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway under the bridge

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must traverse multiple lanes of traffic and a wide median area, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Islands
interventions.description: Install raised, protected refuge islands within the median area under the structure to allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental or ladder-style pavement markings to improve the visibility of the pedestrian crossing area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and bring pedestrians into the driver's line of sight.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and traffic signals in a mixed-use residential area. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals and the presence of parked cars near the crossing reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the right side may block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sight lines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure whose support pillars create significant visual obstructions at the intersection. Although sidewalks are present and in good condition, the absence of marked crosswalks and pedestrian-specific signals increases the risk for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Pillar Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars for the elevated rail structure significantly block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the intersection corners.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway under the elevated structure

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalk markings, leaving pedestrians without a designated or prioritized path across the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility zebra or ladder style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals and improve safety at the signalized intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to move pedestrians past the visual obstruction of the pillars before they enter the roadway, shortening the crossing distance.
